category_title: At-risk eighth-graders with low self-efficacy and negative dispositions toward writing in mathematics
scenario_title: Writing explanations for multi-step word problems in math journals
minimal_context: The student is working independently in math class to solve a multi-step word problem about a parking lot and write the explanation in paragraph form in their math journal.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Please look at the grocery store parking lot problem on the board. I want you to solve it and answer it in paragraph form in your math journals.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Math is numbers not letters. Math and writing don’t go 2-gether.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Just try your best to write down the steps you take to find the answer.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I hate to write expesially in math.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: You need to tell how you solve the problem in writing.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I can’t evn get why she would me make me rite in her class. Nobody has made me tell how I solve problems and never in writing did I have to do this!

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Please look at the grocery store parking lot problem on the board. I want you to solve it and answer it in paragraph form in your math journals.

STUDENT: Math is numbers not letters. Math and writing don’t go 2-gether.

TUTOR: Just try your best to write down the steps you take to find the answer.

STUDENT: I hate to write expesially in math.

TUTOR: You need to tell how you solve the problem in writing.

STUDENT: I can’t evn get why she would me make me rite in her class. Nobody has made me tell how I solve problems and never in writing did I have to do this!

task.content: The grocery store parking lot that will hold 1,000 vehicles, two-ﬁfths of the parking spaces are for cars. When you went to buy groceries, there were 200 cars and some trucks in the parking lot. The parking lot was three-fourths full. How many trucks were in it?

context.materials: word problem on the board, math journals, word wall of math terms

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: Nobody has made them tell how they solve problems and never in writing did they have to do this
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: get easily frustrated, indicated a negative stance toward writing
related_quotes: I can’t evn (even) get why she would me make me rite (write) in her class.
I hate to write expesially (especially) in math.

behavior_patterns.condition: When kids get stuck with spelling
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: they are frozen and cannot move forward until they have the correct spelling

behavior_patterns.condition: as I modeled my own thought process
related_quotes: I thought she was crazy at ﬁrst but now I think out loud all the time.
